QuestionStmt.S: Two simple harmonic motions of angular frequency 300 rad/s and 3000 rad/s have same amplitude. The ratio of their maximum accelerations is

Solution.S:
Let amplitude of both oscillations be $A$.

$$\omega_1 = 300 \text{ rad/s}, \quad \omega_2 = 3000 \text{ rad/s}$$

For SHM, maximum acceleration is $a_{\text{max}} = \omega^2 A$.

$$a_{1,\text{max}} = (300)^2 A = 90000A$$

$$a_{2,\text{max}} = (3000)^2 A = 9000000A$$

$$\frac{a_{1,\text{max}}}{a_{2,\text{max}}} = \frac{90000}{9000000} = \frac{1}{100} = 1 : 100$$

Thus $a_{1,\text{max}} : a_{2,\text{max}} = 1 : 10^2$, which corresponds to option B.
